original_coverage_E: Jakarta Special Capital Region plus the Tangerang conurbation (Tangerang Regency, Tangerang City, South Tangerang City).
coverage_T: Indonesia (Jakarta [entire ADM1], Banten (South Tangerang City, Tangerang City, Tangerang Regency ADM2 only))
changes_vs_old: Tangerang Regency, Tangerang City and South Tangerang City added (old seat was Jakarta only, 11.7m); Depok goes to seat 210.
notes: Contiguous by land (Greater Jakarta). ADM2 names are English forms of BPS names (Regency = kabupaten, City = kota).

original_coverage_E: Bogor Regency and City, Depok City, Sukabumi Regency and City, Cianjur Regency (southern Greater Jakarta and western Priangan).
coverage_T: Indonesia (West Java (Bogor City, Bogor Regency, Cianjur Regency, Depok City, Sukabumi City, Sukabumi Regency ADM2 only))
changes_vs_old: Redrawn: old Bogor-Banten seat lost Banten (Tangerang to 209, rest of Banten to 221) and gained Sukabumi and Cianjur.
notes: Contiguous by land. Regency populations are SP2020 figures grown to 2026 and scaled; individual ADM2 figures approximate.

original_coverage_E: Bandung Regency and City, West Bandung, Cimahi, Sumedang, Garut, Tasikmalaya Regency and City, Ciamis, Pangandaran, Banjar (Bandung basin plus Priangan Timur).
coverage_T: Indonesia (West Java (Bandung City, Bandung Regency, Banjar City, Ciamis Regency, Cimahi City, Garut Regency, Pangandaran Regency, Sumedang Regency, Tasikmalaya City, Tasikmalaya Regency, West Bandung Regency ADM2 only))
changes_vs_old: Boundary set: now includes Priangan Timur (Garut, Tasikmalaya, Ciamis, Pangandaran, Banjar) and Sumedang.

original_coverage_E: Bekasi Regency and City, Karawang, Purwakarta, Subang, Indramayu (north-coast West Java industrial belt).
coverage_T: Indonesia (West Java (Bekasi City, Bekasi Regency, Indramayu Regency, Karawang Regency, Purwakarta Regency, Subang Regency ADM2 only))
changes_vs_old: Subang and Indramayu added to bring the seat into band.
notes: Contiguous by land along the Pantura. Lower-end population (~13m) because the Bogor/Depok and Tangerang parts of Greater Jakarta are in seats 210/209.

original_coverage_E: Cirebon Regency and City, Kuningan, Majalengka plus western Central Java: Brebes, Tegal Regency and City, Pemalang, Banyumas, Cilacap, Purbalingga, Banjarnegara, Kebumen.
coverage_T: Indonesia (West Java (Cirebon City, Cirebon Regency, Kuningan Regency, Majalengka Regency ADM2 only), Central Java (Banjarnegara Regency, Banyumas Regency, Brebes Regency, Cilacap Regency, Kebumen Regency, Pemalang Regency, Purbalingga Regency, Tegal City, Tegal Regency ADM2 only))
changes_vs_old: Redrawn across the West Java/Central Java border (old seat: Cirebon plus eastern West Java); Priangan Timur moved to seat 211.
notes: Contiguous by land. Cirebonese Javanese and Tegal/Banyumas Ngapak dialects form a cultural continuum; needed so that Java (+Lampung) divides into 10 balanced seats.

original_coverage_E: Rest of Central Java: Semarang City and Regency, Salatiga, Demak, Kendal, Batang, Pekalongan Regency and City, Temanggung, Wonosobo, Magelang Regency and City, Purworejo, Kudus, Jepara, Pati, Rembang, Blora, Grobogan.
coverage_T: Indonesia (Central Java (Batang Regency, Blora Regency, Demak Regency, Grobogan Regency, Jepara Regency, Kendal Regency, Kudus Regency, Magelang City, Magelang Regency, Pati Regency, Pekalongan City, Pekalongan Regency, Purworejo Regency, Rembang Regency, Salatiga City, Semarang City, Semarang Regency, Temanggung Regency, Wonosobo Regency ADM2 only))
changes_vs_old: Boundary set to the Central Java remainder after seats 213 and 215.

original_coverage_E: Special Region of Yogyakarta, Surakarta (Solo) area (Surakarta City, Sukoharjo, Karanganyar, Sragen, Klaten, Wonogiri, Boyolali) and the Mataraman west of East Java (Ponorogo, Magetan, Ngawi, Madiun Regency and City, Nganjuk, Kediri Regency and City).
coverage_T: Indonesia (Central Java (Boyolali Regency, Karanganyar Regency, Klaten Regency, Sragen Regency, Sukoharjo Regency, Surakarta City, Wonogiri Regency ADM2 only), Yogyakarta [entire ADM1], East Java (Kediri City, Kediri Regency, Madiun City, Madiun Regency, Magetan Regency, Nganjuk Regency, Ngawi Regency, Ponorogo Regency ADM2 only))
changes_vs_old: Now includes Mataraman districts of western East Java (same Javanese cultural region as Surakarta) to balance East Java population.

original_coverage_E: Surabaya City, Sidoarjo, Gresik, Lamongan, Mojokerto Regency and City, Jombang, Bojonegoro, Tuban and the four Madura regencies (Bangkalan, Sampang, Pamekasan, Sumenep).
coverage_T: Indonesia (East Java (Bangkalan Regency, Bojonegoro Regency, Gresik Regency, Jombang Regency, Lamongan Regency, Mojokerto City, Mojokerto Regency, Pamekasan Regency, Sampang Regency, Sidoarjo Regency, Sumenep Regency, Surabaya City, Tuban Regency ADM2 only))
notes: Contiguous by land; Madura linked by the Suramadu bridge.

original_coverage_E: Malang Regency and City, Batu, Pasuruan Regency and City, Probolinggo Regency and City, Lumajang, Jember, Banyuwangi, Bondowoso, Situbondo, Blitar Regency and City, Tulungagung, Trenggalek, Pacitan.
coverage_T: Indonesia (East Java (Banyuwangi Regency, Batu City, Blitar City, Blitar Regency, Bondowoso Regency, Jember Regency, Lumajang Regency, Malang City, Malang Regency, Pacitan Regency, Pasuruan City, Pasuruan Regency, Probolinggo City, Probolinggo Regency, Situbondo Regency, Trenggalek Regency, Tulungagung Regency ADM2 only))
changes_vs_old: Boundary set explicitly (Tapal Kuda plus south-west fringe).

original_coverage_E: Aceh (entire) plus North Sumatra except the Mandailing-Angkola south-west cluster (Medan, Deli Serdang, Langkat, Karo, Simalungun, Toba Batak lands, Nias islands, etc.).
coverage_T: Indonesia (Aceh [entire ADM1], North Sumatra (Asahan Regency, Batu Bara Regency, Binjai City, Central Tapanuli Regency, Dairi Regency, Deli Serdang Regency, Gunungsitoli City, Humbang Hasundutan Regency, Karo Regency, Labuhanbatu Regency, Langkat Regency, Medan City, Nias Regency, North Labuhanbatu Regency, North Nias Regency, North Tapanuli Regency, Pakpak Bharat Regency, Pematangsiantar City, Samosir Regency, Serdang Bedagai Regency, Sibolga City, Simalungun Regency, South Labuhanbatu Regency, South Nias Regency, Tanjungbalai City, Tebing Tinggi City, Toba Regency, West Nias Regency ADM2 only))
changes_vs_old: Aceh added to North Sumatra (Aceh borders only North Sumatra). Mandailing Natal, South Tapanuli, Padang Lawas, North Padang Lawas and Padang Sidempuan City moved to seat 219 to keep this seat in band.
notes: Contiguous by land; Nias islands (Nias, North/South/West Nias, Gunungsitoli) are linked by regular ferry/air from Sibolga.

original_coverage_E: Riau, Riau Islands and West Sumatra (entire) plus the Mandailing-Angkola cluster of southern North Sumatra (Mandailing Natal, South Tapanuli, Padang Lawas, North Padang Lawas, Padang Sidempuan City).
coverage_T: Indonesia (North Sumatra (Mandailing Natal Regency, North Padang Lawas Regency, Padang Lawas Regency, Padang Sidempuan City, South Tapanuli Regency ADM2 only), West Sumatra [entire ADM1], Riau [entire ADM1], Riau Islands [entire ADM1])
changes_vs_old: Renamed and redrawn: Jambi moved to seat 220; West Sumatra and Mandailing cluster added to Riau (adjacent by land, shared Malay/Minangkabau/Islamic sphere).
notes: Contiguous by land (Riau-West Sumatra-Mandailing). Riau Islands are linked to the Riau coast by short sea routes (Batam/Bintan-Riau ferries).

original_coverage_E: Jambi, Bengkulu, South Sumatra and Bangka Belitung Islands (all entire).
coverage_T: Indonesia (Jambi [entire ADM1], South Sumatra [entire ADM1], Bengkulu [entire ADM1], Bangka Belitung Islands [entire ADM1])
changes_vs_old: Renamed: West Sumatra moved to seat 219, Lampung to seat 221; Jambi, Bengkulu and Bangka Belitung grouped with South Sumatra.
notes: Contiguous by land (Jambi-South Sumatra-Bengkulu). Bangka Belitung is linked to South Sumatra by short sea routes (Muntok-Palembang).

original_coverage_E: Lampung (entire) plus non-metropolitan Banten (Serang Regency and City, Cilegon City, Pandeglang, Lebak).
coverage_T: Indonesia (Lampung [entire ADM1], Banten (Cilegon City, Lebak Regency, Pandeglang Regency, Serang City, Serang Regency ADM2 only))
changes_vs_old: Lampung moved from the old Palembang-Lampung seat and linked to Banten via the Merak-Bakauheni ferry (Java+Lampung then divides into 10 balanced seats; rest of Sumatra into 3).
notes: Link by Sunda Strait ferry (Merak-Bakauheni, ~30 km, established high-frequency route). Lampung has a large Javanese/Sundanese transmigrant population.

original_coverage_E: All five Indonesian Kalimantan provinces (West, Central, South, East, North Kalimantan), including the Nusantara capital area.
coverage_T: Indonesia (West Kalimantan [entire ADM1], Central Kalimantan [entire ADM1], South Kalimantan [entire ADM1], East Kalimantan [entire ADM1], North Kalimantan [entire ADM1])
notes: Contiguous by land. Malaysian Borneo and Brunei are outside this scope.

original_coverage_E: South Sulawesi, Southeast Sulawesi, Central Sulawesi and West Sulawesi (all entire).
coverage_T: Indonesia (Central Sulawesi [entire ADM1], South Sulawesi [entire ADM1], Southeast Sulawesi [entire ADM1], West Sulawesi [entire ADM1])
changes_vs_old: North Sulawesi and Gorontalo moved to seat 225 to keep Sulawesi within band.
notes: Contiguous by land (Southeast Sulawesi borders South and Central Sulawesi on the mainland; Buton islands by short ferry).

original_coverage_E: Bali, West Nusa Tenggara, East Nusa Tenggara (all entire) plus all of Timor-Leste.
coverage_T: Indonesia (Bali [entire ADM1], West Nusa Tenggara [entire ADM1], East Nusa Tenggara [entire ADM1]); Timor-Leste [entire ADM0]
notes: Island chain linked by short ferry routes (Bali-Lombok-Sumbawa-Flores); West Timor (East Nusa Tenggara) borders Timor-Leste by land. Timor-Leste: 2022 census grown to 2026 (~1.42m).

original_coverage_E: Maluku, North Maluku, all six Papua-region provinces (Papua, South Papua, Central Papua, Highland Papua, West Papua, Southwest Papua), North Sulawesi and Gorontalo.
coverage_T: Indonesia (North Sulawesi [entire ADM1], Gorontalo [entire ADM1], Maluku [entire ADM1], North Maluku [entire ADM1], Papua [entire ADM1], South Papua [entire ADM1], Central Papua [entire ADM1], Highland Papua [entire ADM1], West Papua [entire ADM1], Southwest Papua [entire ADM1])
changes_vs_old: North Sulawesi and Gorontalo added from the Sulawesi seat to lift this seat out of the LOW range; Papua region counted as six provinces.
notes: Long sea links: North Maluku-North Sulawesi (Ternate-Bitung/Manado, ~400 km; Morotai and Talaud are close to Minahasa; Pelni ferries/flights) and Maluku-Papua (Seram/Kei/Aru to Papua). Papua population uncertain (2020 census issues, new provinces). If the GIS layer has the old 34 provinces, Papua (4 new) and West Papua (2 new) map to the same units.
